brief: The VIX term structure has steepened as front-end implied volatility collapsed since the start of the Iran war while the back end stays elevated, producing what the author calls a volatility deficit implying an eventual reckoning for stocks. SPX has gone 23 consecutive trading days without a 1% decline, near the 90th percentile of a three-year lookback, aided by the Citadel/Aschenbrenner deleveraging in late July, which washed out crowded momentum positioning and stabilized gamma dynamics. The note contrasts this with the comparable prior streak (early May to mid-July 2024): that episode coincided with a dovish Fed hold, markets pricing roughly 75bp of cuts by year-end, and the 10-year yield falling about 40bp, giving equities a rates tailwind. Today's SPX/10-year correlation is similarly negative (-0.41 vs -0.47 then), but the note says yields are moving in the opposite direction now, so that rates support is absent. Longer-dated VIX still carries a premium, implying the market is deferring volatility rather than eliminating it, and the next steep selloff could be the trigger for the deferred deficit coming due.
